ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: Tips for Making a Habit Stick

fullPassage:
Tips for Making a Habit Stick

Forming a new habit is not easy, especially in the beginning. Here are five ways to start a habit that really sticks. First, start small. Don't try to do too much, too quickly. A habit is formed through repetition, so make the change easier to repeat. Second, make your goal specific. Don't say, "I'll meditate regularly." Say, "I'll meditate for five minutes each day." This works even better if you combine your new habit with an existing one, for example, "After brushing my teeth in the morning, I'll meditate for five minutes." When your fixed habit becomes a cue for action, your new habit is more likely to stick. Third, make it attractive. Pair your new change with what you love. You could listen to your favorite piece of calming music while meditating. Fourth, track your progress. Mark a calendar with an X every time you finish something. Seeing the progress gives you a sense of achievement and helps you keep going. Fifth, be flexible. Forming a new habit takes time. If you find that your progress has stopped for any reason, just pick up where you left off.

questions.passage: Forming a new habit is not easy, especially in the beginning. Here are five ways to start a habit that really sticks. First, start small. Don't try to do too much, too quickly. A habit is formed through (A)[repetition / innovation], so make the change easier to repeat. Second, make your goal (B)[specific / vague]. Don't say, "I'll meditate regularly." Say, "I'll meditate for five minutes each day." This works even better if you (C)[combine / separate] your new habit with an existing one.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 습관은 반복(repetition)을 통해 형성되므로, 목표를 구체적으로(specific) 설정하고, 기존 습관과 결합(combine)하라.
det.analysis:
✅ ① repetition — specific — combine: 원문 그대로
❌ ② innovation(혁신): repetition(반복)의 반의어
❌ ③ vague(막연한): specific(구체적인)의 반의어
❌ ④ 모두 원문과 반대
det.tip: repetition(반복) ↔ innovation(혁신). specific(구체적) ↔ vague(막연한). combine(결합) ↔ separate(분리)

questions.passage: When your fixed habit becomes a cue for action, your new habit is more likely to stick. Third, make it (A)[attractive / repulsive]. Pair your new change with what you love. You could listen to your favorite piece of calming music while meditating. Fourth, track your (B)[progress / failure]. Mark a calendar with an X every time you finish something. Seeing the progress gives you a sense of (C)[achievement / defeat] and helps you keep going.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 새 습관을 매력적으로(attractive) 만들고, 진행 상황(progress)을 추적하면 성취감(achievement)을 얻을 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② attractive — progress — achievement: 원문 그대로
❌ ① repulsive(거슬리는): attractive의 반의어
❌ ③ failure(실패): progress(진행)의 반의어
❌ ④ 모두 원문과 반대
det.tip: attractive(매력적인) ↔ repulsive(역겨운). achievement(성취) ↔ defeat(패배)

questions.passage: Don't say, "I'll meditate (A)[regularly / occasionally]." Say, "I'll meditate for five minutes each day." This works even better if you combine your new habit with an existing one, for example, "After brushing my teeth in the morning, I'll meditate for five minutes." When your (B)[fixed / random] habit becomes a (C)[cue / barrier] for action, your new habit is more likely to stick.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: '규칙적으로(regularly) 명상하겠다'고 막연하게 말하지 마라. 고정된(fixed) 습관이 행동의 신호(cue)가 되면 새 습관이 정착된다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ regularly — fixed — cue: 원문 그대로
❌ ① occasionally(가끔): regularly(규칙적으로)의 반의어
❌ ② random(무작위): fixed(고정된)의 반의어
❌ ③ 모두 원문과 반대
det.tip: cue(신호/단서) — 행동을 유발하는 자극. fixed habit → cue → new habit sticks

questions.passage: Forming a new habit is not easy, especially in the beginning. Here are five ways to start a habit that really sticks. First, start ①<u>small</u>. Don't try to do too much, too quickly. A habit is formed through ②<u>repetition</u>, so make the change easier to repeat. Second, make your goal ③<u>specific</u>. Fourth, track your ④<u>failures</u>. Mark a calendar with an X every time you finish something.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ failures(실패) → progress(진행 상황). 원문: 'track your progress'(진행 상황을 추적하라). 완료할 때마다 표시하는 긍정적 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ④ failures: 원문은 progress(진행 상황). 완료 표시를 하는 긍정 맥락에 failures 부적절
❌ ① small(작게): 원문 그대로
❌ ② repetition(반복): 원문 그대로
❌ ③ specific(구체적인): 원문 그대로
det.tip: progress(진행 상황) ↔ failures(실패). track your progress = 진행 상황을 추적하다

questions.passage: This works even better if you combine your new habit with an ①<u>existing</u> one. When your fixed habit becomes a ②<u>cue</u> for action, your new habit is more likely to stick. Third, make it ③<u>attractive</u>. Pair your new change with what you love. Fifth, be ④<u>rigid</u>. Forming a new habit takes time.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ rigid(경직된) → flexible(유연한). 원문: 'Fifth, be flexible.' 새 습관 형성에 시간이 걸리므로 유연하게 대처하라는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ④ rigid: 원문은 flexible(유연한). 중단 시 다시 시작하라는 맥락에 rigid(경직된) 부적절
❌ ① existing(기존의): 원문 그대로
❌ ② cue(신호): 원문 그대로
❌ ③ attractive(매력적인): 원문 그대로
det.tip: flexible(유연한) ↔ rigid(경직된). be flexible = 융통성 있게 행동하다

questions.passage: Don't say, "I'll meditate regularly." Say, "I'll meditate for five minutes each day." This works even better if you combine your new habit with an existing one. When your fixed habit becomes a cue for action, your new habit is more likely to ①<u>stick</u>. Third, make it attractive. ②<u>Pair</u> your new change with what you love. Seeing the ③<u>decline</u> gives you a sense of achievement and helps you keep going. Fifth, be flexible. If you find that your progress has stopped, just ④<u>pick up</u> where you left off.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ decline(감소) → progress(진행). 원문: 'Seeing the progress gives you a sense of achievement.' 성취감을 주는 것은 '진행 상황'이지 '감소'가 아님.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ③ decline: 원문은 progress(진행). 성취감을 주는 맥락에 decline(감소) 부적절
❌ ① stick(정착되다): 원문 그대로
❌ ② Pair(짝짓다): 원문 그대로
❌ ④ pick up(다시 시작하다): 원문 그대로
det.tip: progress(진행/발전) ↔ decline(감소/하락). pick up where you left off = 중단한 곳에서 다시 시작하다

questions.passage: Forming a new habit is not easy, especially in the beginning. Here are five ways to start a habit that really sticks. First, start small. Don't try to do too much, too quickly. A habit is formed through __________, so make the change easier to repeat.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 습관은 반복(repetition)을 통해 형성되므로 변화를 더 반복하기 쉽게 만들라.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ repetition: 원문 'formed through repetition' 그대로. repeat와 연결
❌ ① imagination(상상력): 문맥 무관
❌ ② competition(경쟁): 문맥 무관
❌ ④ destruction(파괴): 문맥 반대
det.tip: repetition(반복). repeat(반복하다)와 같은 어근. -tion: 명사 어미

questions.passage: Don't say, "I'll meditate regularly." Say, "I'll meditate for five minutes each day." This works even better if you combine your new habit with an existing one, for example, "After brushing my teeth in the morning, I'll meditate for five minutes." When your fixed habit becomes a __________ for action, your new habit is more likely to stick.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 고정된 습관이 행동의 신호(cue)가 되면 새 습관은 정착될 가능성이 높다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① cue: 원문 'a cue for action' 그대로. 행동을 유발하는 신호
❌ ② obstacle(장애물): 행동을 막는 것
❌ ③ punishment(처벌): 문맥 반대
❌ ④ reward(보상): 유사하지만 cue(신호)와 다름
det.tip: cue(신호/단서) — 특정 행동을 시작하게 하는 trigger. habit loop: cue → routine → reward

questions.passage: Fourth, track your progress. Mark a calendar with an X every time you finish something. Seeing the progress gives you a sense of __________ and helps you keep going. Fifth, be flexible. Forming a new habit takes time. If you find that your progress has stopped for any reason, just pick up where you left off.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 진행 상황을 보는 것이 성취감(achievement)을 주고 계속하도록 도와준다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② achievement: 원문 'a sense of achievement' 그대로
❌ ① guilt(죄책감): 긍정 맥락에 부적합
❌ ③ exhaustion(탈진): 부정적 의미
❌ ④ isolation(고립): 문맥 무관
det.tip: a sense of achievement = 성취감. 진행 표시(X)를 보면서 동기 부여

questions.passage: Forming a new habit is not easy, especially in the beginning. Here are five ways to start a habit that really sticks. First, start small. Don't try to do too much, too <u>quickly</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 quickly의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: quickly = 빠르게, rapidly = 빠르게 (동의어)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ rapidly(빠르게): quickly의 동의어
❌ ① slowly(천천히): 반의어
❌ ② carefully(조심스럽게): 의미 다름
❌ ③ gradually(점차): 의미 다름
det.tip: quickly(빠르게) = rapidly = fast. 반의어: slowly, gradually

questions.passage: Third, make it attractive. Pair your new change with what you love. You could listen to your favorite piece of calming music while meditating. Fourth, track your progress. Mark a calendar with an X every time you <u>finish</u> something.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 finish의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: finish = 끝마치다, complete = 완료하다 (동의어)
det.analysis:
✅ ① complete(완료하다): finish의 동의어
❌ ② abandon(포기하다): 반의어
❌ ③ postpone(연기하다): 의미 다름
❌ ④ ignore(무시하다): 의미 다름
det.tip: finish(끝내다) = complete = accomplish. 반의어: abandon, quit

questions.passage: When your fixed habit becomes a cue for action, your new habit is more likely to stick. Third, make it <u>attractive</u>. Pair your new change with what you love.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 attractive의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: attractive = 매력적인, appealing = 매력적인 (동의어)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ appealing(매력적인): attractive의 동의어
❌ ① boring(지루한): 반의어
❌ ② difficult(어려운): 의미 다름
❌ ④ exhausting(지치는): 의미 다름
det.tip: attractive(매력적인) = appealing = charming. 반의어: unattractive, repulsive

questions.passage: Second, make your goal specific. Don't say, "I'll meditate regularly." Say, "I'll meditate for five minutes each day." This works even better if you combine your new habit with an <u>existing</u> one.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 existing의 의미와 가장 반대되는 것은?

det.korean: existing = 기존의, new = 새로운 (반의어)
det.analysis:
✅ ② new(새로운): existing(기존의)의 반의어
❌ ① current(현재의): existing과 유사어
❌ ③ present(현재의): existing과 유사어
❌ ④ established(확립된): existing과 유사어
det.tip: existing(기존의) = current = established ↔ new(새로운). 오답이 모두 유사어라 혼동 주의

questions.passage: Fifth, be <u>flexible</u>. Forming a new habit takes time. If you find that your progress has stopped for any reason, just pick up where you left off.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 flexible의 의미와 가장 반대되는 것은?

det.korean: flexible = 유연한, inflexible = 유연하지 않은 (반의어)
det.analysis:
✅ ① inflexible(유연하지 않은): flexible의 직접적 반의어
❌ ② adaptable(적응력 있는): flexible과 유사어
❌ ③ versatile(다재다능한): flexible과 유사어
❌ ④ adjustable(조정 가능한): flexible과 유사어
det.tip: flexible(유연한) = adaptable = versatile ↔ inflexible = rigid = stiff. 접두사 in- = 부정

questions.passage:
(A) Here are five ways to start a habit that really <u>sticks</u>.
(B) Mark a calendar with an X every time you finish something. Seeing the progress gives you a sense of achievement and helps you keep going. If you find that your progress has stopped, just pick up where you left off — grab a <u>stick</u> and draw your X again!
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 stick(s)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) a habit that really sticks = 정말 정착하는(sticks) 습관 — 동사 (B) grab a stick = 막대기(stick)를 잡다 — 명사
det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) 정착하다 – (B) 막대기: (A)는 동사(정착하다), (B)는 명사(막대기)
❌ ① 순서 반대
❌ ② 둘 다 정착: (B)는 명사 용법
❌ ④ 둘 다 막대기: (A)는 동사 용법
det.tip: stick: 동사(정착하다/붙다) vs 명사(막대기). make a habit stick = 습관을 정착시키다

questions.stem:
다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"to join or put together two or more things"

det.korean: "두 가지 이상의 것을 합치거나 결합하다" = combine(결합하다)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ combine(결합하다): 두 가지 이상을 합치는 것
❌ ① separate(분리하다): combine의 반의어
❌ ② eliminate(제거하다): 의미 다름
❌ ③ distinguish(구별하다): 의미 다름
det.tip: combine(결합하다) = merge = unite. 반의어: separate, divide

questions.passage: A habit is formed through repetition, so make the change easier to repeat. Second, make your goal specific. Don't say, "I'll meditate __________. (regular)"
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: '나는 규칙적으로(regularly) 명상을 할 거야'라고 말하지 마라.
det.analysis: ✅ regularly: 동사 meditate를 수식하는 부사 필요. regular(형용사) → regularly(부사)
det.tip: regular(형용사) → regularly(부사). 동사 수식 = 부사 형태

questions.passage: Fourth, track your progress. Mark a calendar with an X every time you finish something. Seeing the progress gives you a sense of __________ and helps you keep going. (achieve)
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 진행 상황을 보는 것이 성취감(achievement)을 준다.
det.analysis: ✅ achievement: a sense of + 명사 구조. achieve(동사) → achievement(명사)
det.tip: achieve(동사) → achievement(명사). a sense of + 명사: ~감, ~의식

questions.passage: Third, make it attractive. Pair your new change with what you love. You could listen to your favorite piece of calming music while meditating. Fourth, track your progress. Mark a calendar with an X every time you finish something. Seeing the progress gives you a sense of achievement and helps you __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 성취감이 계속 나아가도록(keep going) 도와준다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ keep going: 원문 'helps you keep going' 그대로
❌ ① give up(포기하다): 성취감의 효과와 반대
❌ ② fall behind(뒤처지다): 문맥 반대
❌ ④ start over(처음부터 다시): 유사하지만 원문과 다름
det.tip: keep going = 계속하다. 성취감(achievement) → 동기 부여 → keep going

questions.passage: Fifth, be flexible. Forming a new habit takes time. If you find that your progress has stopped for any reason, just __________ where you left off. Don't give up entirely — the key is to resume when you're ready.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 중단된 지점에서 그저 다시 시작하라(pick up).
det.analysis:
✅ ② pick up: 원문 'pick up where you left off' 그대로. 중단한 곳에서 다시 시작
❌ ① break down(고장나다/무너지다): 부정적 의미
❌ ③ turn away(외면하다): 문맥 반대
❌ ④ hold back(망설이다): 문맥 반대
det.tip: pick up where you left off = 중단한 곳에서 다시 시작하다. 관용 표현 암기 필수
